name: Adjuvant Olaparib (OlympiA)
cyclesNote: 1 year (12 cycles of 28 days). Administered following completion of definitive surgery, adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and radiation therapy.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026
source.primaryStudy: OlympiA: Tutt ANJ, Garber JE, Kaufman B, et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405; Geyer CE, et al. Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-M 2, 3, 5 of 10)

biomarkers.note: Requires documented deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic variant AND high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer: for TNBC, primary tumor ≥2 cm or positive lymph nodes after surgery, OR residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy; for HR+/HER2-, ≥4 pathologically involved lymph nodes after surgery, OR residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy with clinical-pathologic stage + estrogen-receptor + grade (CPS+EG) score ≥3. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer v6.2026, BINV-M 2, 3, and 5 of 10 (Category 1).

histology: invasive breast carcinoma (TNBC or HR-positive / HER2-negative)
supportiveCare: Sequencing with Radiation Therapy: Olaparib should be given AFTER completion of adjuvant radiation therapy (not concurrently).
Partner therapy: In HR-positive disease, adjuvant olaparib may be given concurrently with adjuvant endocrine therapy.
Hematologic monitoring: Monitor for severe cytopenias (anemia is common; transfusions may be required).
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) / Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) vigilance: Monitor for prolonged cytopenias.
monitoring: CBC with differential at baseline and monthly thereafter
Renal function tests (BUN, serum creatinine) at baseline and periodically
Monitor for symptoms of severe fatigue, nausea, vomiting, or recurrent infections
clearanceChecks: renal function (estimated CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min; reduce dose if moderate renal impairment)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 or 4 hematologic toxicity (severe anemia Hb < 8 g/dL, ANC < 1000/mcL, or platelets < 50,000/mcL)
doseModificationRules.text: Hold olaparib until blood counts recover. Resume at reduced dose: first reduction 250 mg PO BID; second reduction 200 mg PO BID. If counts remain abnormal after 4 weeks of hold, evaluate for MDS/AML with bone marrow examination.
Reduce olaparib dose to 200 mg PO twice daily.
Hold until resolution to grade ≤ 1; resume at 250 mg PO BID.

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026, BINV-M 5 of 10. Olaparib 300 mg PO twice daily on Days 1 to 28 of 28-day cycle for 1 year (12 cycles).
